post_closure_amendments.mechanism_correction_appended_at_dc08c17: RECORD-ONLY CORRECTION (Family 4, LOW): this block's symbol note 'removed-cycle self-root fallback' and the original _local_delete_effects docstring described the fallback as PER-MEMBER self-root tombstones. The bytes implement (and always implemented at dc08c17): the FIRST uncovered member of a removed ring component (before-list order) becomes the component's root tombstone and claims its removed-descendant chain; LATER ring members become descendant markers naming that root. The two variants differ observably for an offered-alive ring member; the shipped (weaker, F-3-consistent) form is CANONICAL. Locked by test_removed_cycle_fallback_roots_component_once (fails under a per-member self-root mutation). Zero production-behavior change.
post_closure_amendments.correction: The prior amendment's claim 'without touching nodes outside the subtree' (and the matching work-order postcondition claim) was FALSIFIED at 3360c43: derive_transition_effects emitted an independent delete tombstone for every locally-removed id, so a descendant that had escaped the subtree before the delete committed was matched by its own tombstone, removed from every future offer, and its tombstone never retired — permanent, refresh-immune removal of a live node. Delete authority is now ROOT-SCOPED: root tombstones own exactly the offered subtree beneath their root; descendant markers are compositional only (they retire the descendant's earlier create/fields effects) and never remove or pin an offered node. RECORD CORRECTION carried with this amendment: the 3360c43 result's pre-fix mutation evidence stated eight failing tests; the correct count is nine — test_overlay_composition_rules also fails against 7d8e7cd. CF-S03CR-10 remains OPEN pending independent audit.
